# syllabus-calendar-mcp

> Syllabus to calendar MCP server. Extract dated events from syllabus text, build valid .ics calendars from events and recurring classes, expand classes with holidays and reading weeks skipped, and merge calendars while checking for conflicts. Works offline, no account.

## Setup
- Run with npx -y syllabus-calendar-mcp
- Works offline, no account. No environment variables, no network calls and no data is stored.
- Tools: extract_schedule_events, expand_recurring_classes, build_ics, merge_calendars.

## When to use

Use this server when a student wants course dates turned into a calendar, or wants an existing calendar file cleaned up. The request usually mentions a syllabus, a course outline, a class schedule, a reading week or an .ics file.

- A student pastes syllabus or course outline text and asks for the dates, deadlines or exam days: call extract_schedule_events, then build_ics if they also want a calendar file.
- A student describes a class that meets on set days and wants every meeting added, with a holiday or reading week skipped: call expand_recurring_classes.
- A student asks for an .ics file, a calendar to import, or reminders before deadlines: call build_ics with the events and classes.
- A student has several course calendars and wants one merged file, or wants to know which classes overlap: call merge_calendars.
- A student wants to fetch a syllabus from D2L Brightspace first: our brightspace-d2l-mcp server can read the course, then this server can turn the text into calendar events.

This server works on text the student pastes or a calendar file they provide. It does not log in to a school system or fetch course data on its own.

## Tools

### extract_schedule_events
Extract dated events from pasted syllabus text. Each line that names a date becomes one event, with a title, a type, a date and optional times. Inputs: text (the pasted syllabus or course schedule, one event per line), course (a course name or code to put on every event), year (the year to use when a date has no year) and term_start (the first day of the term, so a line such as Week 5: Midterm becomes an event). Titles are read from the words around the date, and each event is marked as an assignment, exam, quiz, lab, reading, class or other. Any line that has no date is returned in undated_lines instead of being dropped. The answer ends with a next step hint that points to build_ics when the events should become a calendar. Example prompt: "Turn this syllabus into calendar events: Assignment 1 due Sep 15, Midterm exam October 20 at 10:00."

Parameters: text (string, required), course (string, optional), year (number, optional), term_start (string, optional).
- text (string, required): The pasted syllabus or course schedule. Put one event on each line, with a date on the line.
- course (string, optional): Course name or code to put on every event, such as BIO 101.
- year (number, optional): The year to use when a date has no year. Defaults to the current year.
- term_start (string, optional): First day of the term as YYYY-MM-DD. When set, a line like Week 5: Midterm with no date becomes an event on the first day of week 5, where week 1 starts on this date.

Example call: {"name":"extract_schedule_events","arguments":{"text":"Assignment 1 due Sep 15\nMidterm exam October 20 at 10:00","course":"BIO 101"}}
Output: Two events found.

- Sep 15, 2026: Assignment 1 (assignment) [BIO 101]
- Oct 20, 2026 at 10:00: Midterm exam (exam) [BIO 101]
Structured output: events, count, year, undated_lines

### expand_recurring_classes
Generate the meeting dates for a recurring class between two dates, and skip holidays and reading weeks. Inputs: course, weekdays (day names or codes such as Tuesday or TU), start_date, end_date, start_time, optional end_time, optional location, holidays (single dates or ranges) and reading_weeks (single dates or ranges). Returns every meeting date plus the dates that were skipped and why. The answer ends with a next step hint that points to build_ics when the class should become a calendar. Example prompt: "My biology class meets Tuesday and Thursday from Sep 8 to Dec 10, 2026 at 10:00. Skip the reading week of Oct 12 to Oct 16."

Parameters: course (string, required), title (string, optional), weekdays (array, required), start_date (string, required), end_date (string, required), start_time (string, required), end_time (string, optional), location (string, optional), holidays (array, optional), reading_weeks (array, optional).
- course (string, required): Course name or code, such as BIO 101.
- title (string, optional): Title for the calendar event. Defaults to the course name plus class.
- weekdays (array, required): Days the class meets, as names or codes, such as "Tuesday", "Tue" or "TU".
- start_date (string, required): First date of the term as YYYY-MM-DD.
- end_date (string, required): Last date of the term as YYYY-MM-DD.
- start_time (string, required): Class start time as HH:MM or 2:30 PM.
- end_time (string, optional): Class end time as HH:MM or 2:30 PM. It must be after start_time.
- location (string, optional): Room or place.
- holidays (array, optional): Holiday dates or ranges, such as "2026-10-12" or "2026-10-12 to 2026-10-16".
- reading_weeks (array, optional): Reading week dates or ranges, such as "2026-10-12 to 2026-10-16".

Example call: {"name":"expand_recurring_classes","arguments":{"course":"BIO 101","weekdays":["Tuesday","Thursday"],"start_date":"2026-09-08","end_date":"2026-12-10","start_time":"10:00","reading_weeks":["2026-10-12 to 2026-10-16"]}}
Output: 24 class meetings for BIO 101 from Sep 08, 2026 to Dec 10, 2026.

- Tue Sep 08, 2026 10:00
- Thu Sep 10, 2026 10:00

Skipped:

- Mon Oct 12, 2026 (reading week)
- Tue Oct 13, 2026 (reading week)
Structured output: course, title, weekdays, start_date, end_date, start_time, end_time, location, meetings, skipped, candidate_count

### build_ics
Build a valid .ics calendar file from dated events and recurring classes, with reminders. Inputs: events (each with title, date, optional start_time, end_time, type, course, location and notes), classes (each with course, weekdays, start_date, end_date, start_time and optional end_time, location, holidays and reading_weeks), reminders_minutes (whole minutes before each event, default 60), calendar_name and optional output_path. Each class becomes one weekly recurring event with holidays and reading weeks removed. The tool checks the file before returning it. Example prompt: "Make an .ics file for my course with a reminder one day before each assignment."

Parameters: events (array, optional), classes (array, optional), reminders_minutes (array, optional), calendar_name (string, optional), output_path (string, optional).
- events (array, optional): Dated events such as assignments and exams.
- classes (array, optional): Recurring classes to add as weekly events.
- reminders_minutes (array, optional): Reminder times in whole minutes before an event. Defaults to [60].
- calendar_name (string, optional): Name shown in the calendar app. Defaults to "Course calendar".
- output_path (string, optional): Optional file path for the .ics file. The folder must already exist because folders are not created. Leave it out to get the calendar text back instead.

Example call: {"name":"build_ics","arguments":{"events":[{"title":"Assignment 1","type":"assignment","date":"2026-09-15"}],"reminders_minutes":[1440]}}
Output: Built a calendar with 1 event, 0 classes and 0 class meetings. The file passed every check.
Structured output: ics, event_count, class_count, class_meetings, valid, errors, output_path

### merge_calendars
Merge several course calendars into one and list timed events that overlap. Inputs: calendars (each with an optional name and an ics string), optional calendar_name and optional output_path. Events with the same UID are kept once. Weekly and daily recurring events are expanded when conflicts are checked. Example prompt: "Merge my three course calendars and tell me which classes conflict."

Parameters: calendars (array, required), calendar_name (string, optional), output_path (string, optional).
- calendars (array, required): The calendars to merge, each with the calendar text and an optional name.
- calendar_name (string, optional): Name for the merged calendar. Defaults to "Merged course calendar".
- output_path (string, optional): Optional file path for the .ics file. The folder must already exist because folders are not created. Leave it out to get the calendar text back instead.

Example call: {"name":"merge_calendars","arguments":{"calendars":[{"name":"BIO 101","ics":"BEGIN:VCALENDAR\nVERSION:2.0\nPRODID:-//AnonymousOnyx22//syllabus-calendar-mcp//EN\nBEGIN:VEVENT\nUID:test1@syllabus-calendar-mcp\nDTSTAMP:20260101T000000Z\nDTSTART:20260915T100000\nDTEND:20260915T110000\nSUMMARY:Class\nEND:VEVENT\nEND:VCALENDAR"}],"calendar_name":"Merged"}}
Output: Merged 1 event from 1 calendar.

No timed events overlap.
Structured output: ics, event_count, calendar_count, conflicts, valid, errors, output_path
